name: issue_boot_io_request
description: Boot block entry that issues one exec input/output request through the DoIO library call. The decompiler timed out, so only that call, the instruction count and the boot entry point are shown.

name: refill_bit_reader_longword
description: Reads the longword just before its input pointer and returns it shifted right one bit with the top bit set. It also stores a two-byte value built from the low byte of that longword and the high byte of another register to a fixed output cell.

name: advance_bit_buffer_by_count
description: Shifts a bit buffer right one bit per iteration for the number of times given in a count register, calling the refill routine whenever the buffer runs out. It writes no output of its own.

name: return_stack_longword
description: Returns the longword at the top of the stack unchanged; the decoded body is only two instructions. It was reached only as a gap in the decoded segment, so no caller is confirmed.

name: program_audio_channel_three_dma
description: Sets the audio channel three location register and writes the DMA control, interrupt enable and interrupt request registers, using the set-bit convention for enables. The decompiler timed out, so only this register use is shown.

key: batman returns (1993)(gametek)[cr qtx](disk 1 of 2)/Batman Returns (1993)(GameTek)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 2).adf:bootblock:0:000C
name: allocate_buffer_and_dispatch
description: Boot block entry that disables task switching, enters supervisor state and allocates a memory buffer through the exec library. It then issues repeated I/O requests until a status byte clears, and finally calls code at the address returned by the allocation.

key: Batman Returns (1993)(GameTek)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$1600 to $070000 (5632 bytes):0:0024
name: decompress_packed_stream_backward
description: Unpacks a compressed stream into memory, filling from the end of the output area toward its start with the bit-reader routines supplying control bits, lengths and literal bytes. Each control bit selects either a copy of bytes already written or a single literal byte, and the routine also touches the background colour register.

key: Batman Returns (1993)(GameTek)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$3C00 to $002800 (10240 bytes):0:0000
name: copy_handler_block_to_ram
description: Clears all interrupt enables and requests and disables DMA channels through the custom chip registers, then copies a block of 128 bytes of code to a fixed RAM address. It stores an entry pointer to the copy in a fixed RAM cell and calls three unnamed routines.

key: Batman Returns (1993)(GameTek)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$3C00 to $002800 (10240 bytes):0:0046
name: copy_overlapping_block_then_patch
description: Copies about ten thousand bytes into place, choosing the direction by comparing source and destination so overlapping data is not overwritten, then modifies two words in place. The decoded tail is invalid instruction data, so the routine's final state is unreliable.

key: Batman Returns (1993)(GameTek)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$3C00 to $002800 (10240 bytes):0:0064
name: copy_block_backward_then_patch
description: Copies a block one byte at a time from its end toward its start, using the count and two base addresses from registers, then modifies two words in place. The decoded tail is invalid instruction data, so the routine's final state is unreliable.

key: Batman Returns (1993)(GameTek)[cr QTX](Disk 1 of 2).adf boot-block load +$3C00 to $002800 (10240 bytes):0:0074
name: probe_ram_marker_then_call
description: Stores a fixed test value in one RAM cell, then checks whether a second RAM cell holds it. If it does, the routine calls an exec library entry through a base pointer and returns bits 16 to 23 of the result; otherwise it returns the test value.

name: store_values_into_two_blocks
description: Writes a longword to two pointed-to areas, two words into the second area and a longword into the next slot of each area, all taken from registers. It has no calls and no further control flow.

name: fill_table_and_relink_lists
description: Fills eight consecutive longword cells with one constant, then moves pointer entries between two chains depending on a flag and relinks their neighbours. The listed facts show no library calls or hardware registers.

name: build_register_pair_list
description: Writes a sequence of address and value word pairs into a RAM buffer: a fixed set of pairs, eight pairs with incrementing values, a 32-word block copied from another table, four pairs holding a computed address split into upper and lower halves, and an end marker pair. The listed facts show no calls and no hardware writes inside this routine.

name: poll_flag_with_bounded_wait
description: Calls an unnamed routine up to two thousand five hundred times in a counted loop, returning early as soon as bit four of a RAM flag is set. It acts as a bounded wait for that flag.

name: set_flag_then_wait_loop
description: Sets a RAM flag to all ones, calls two unnamed routines, then calls a further unnamed routine 350 times in a counted loop.

name: wrap_unnamed_routine_call
description: Makes a single call to a fixed unnamed routine and returns, with no other work in the decoded body. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: service_audio_voice_state
description: Clears the audio control bits and calls three unnamed routines, then steps a per-voice state byte: a pending value enables DMA and resets the voice counters, an idle state zeroes a channel volume register, and the remaining states call further unnamed routines. The listed facts also show disk and serial register use.

name: advance_voice_state_record
description: Runs the same pending-value step as the global voice handler on a voice record passed by pointer: a pending value enables DMA and resets counters in the record, an idle state zeroes a field in the record, and other states call unnamed routines. It is called by two unnamed routines.

name: interpret_sequence_commands
description: Reads command bytes from a sequence stream: bytes with the top bit clear set a countdown and end the call, while bytes with the top bit set either set fields in the record, store loop and jump values, or change its state. It stops reading once the stream reaches its end command.

name: initialize_voice_record_fields
description: Clears a block of fields in a voice record, sets a few to initial values such as a full-scale word and small counters, and zeroes a related word through a second pointer. It calls one unnamed routine and is called by two.

name: copy_voice_word_to_register
description: Copies one word from a voice record field into a register addressed from a base pointer, and into another field of the record. The routine has three instructions and one unnamed caller.

name: update_scaled_level_and_timer
description: Computes a scaled level from two record fields and stores its low byte in another field, then reduces a countdown by a fixed amount. When the countdown reaches zero it clears four state bytes spaced ten apart in a shared block.

name: advance_level_ramp_state
description: Advances a five-state ramp kept in a voice record: depending on the current state it lowers a level toward a floor, raises it by a step until it passes a fixed ceiling, holds it, steps a second byte toward a target, or sets the level to a stored end value. The code shows only these record updates and no hardware access.

name: step_level_toward_limit
description: Moves a level word in a voice record toward a limit by a per-record step, stopping at the limit in either direction; a zero step copies the limit directly into the level.

name: read_next_signed_table_value
description: Reads the next signed byte from a table indexed by a record offset, backing up one entry whenever it reads the end-marker value 127 so the value is not taken. It stores the value in a record word and advances the index, wrapping it at a stored limit.

name: read_timed_table_value_step
description: Counts down a record counter and, when it reaches zero, reloads it and reads the next signed table value into a record word scaled by eight. The table index backs up at the end-marker value and wraps at a stored limit.

name: store_scaled_value_and_advance
description: Stores a register value shifted left three bits into a record word, then advances the record's table index and wraps it at a stored limit. It has one unnamed caller and calls one more unnamed routine.

name: clear_record_index_byte
description: Sets one byte at a fixed offset in a record to zero and returns. Two unnamed routines call it.

name: store_summed_level_word
description: Adds two signed bytes from a voice record to the low seven bits of a register, keeps the result as a byte, shifts it left four bits and stores it in a record word. It has one unnamed caller.

name: split_index_and_lookup_word
description: Adds four record values and a constant, divides the total by 96, and uses the remainder as an index into a word table. It shifts that word right by the quotient and stores half of the result in a second structure.

name: reset_hardware_and_relocate_code

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:$00000000:0:002C
name: unpack_run_length_stream
description: Copies an input stream into memory, expanding each run marker byte value 217 into repeated copies of the byte that follows it, until the source reaches a fixed end address. It records the current input position in a pointer cell and then clears three custom chip control registers.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:$00000000:0:0072
name: decode_bitstream_then_expand_runs
description: Decodes a bit-packed stream into memory using bit-reader calls, a lookup table and back-references, then expands run markers as a forward unpacker does. It writes the input position to a pointer cell and clears three custom chip control registers at the end.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:$00000000:0:00B2
name: refill_bit_buffer_store_word

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:$00000000:0:0196
name: discard_bits_from_buffer
description: Shifts a bit buffer right one bit per iteration for the count given in a register, calling the refill routine when the buffer empties, so the caller discards that many bits. It is called by five unnamed routines.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:$00000000:0:01B0
name: reset_hardware_and_copy_block

name: copy_code_block_then_call
description: Copies about 650 bytes of its own code to a fixed RAM address, sets two fixed RAM cells, and calls through a pointer stored in RAM. The listed facts also show a background colour register write.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:$00000001:0:002C
name: unpack_runs_to_low_ram
description: Expands run marker bytes into memory beginning at a low fixed address, copying the stream until the source reaches a fixed end address. It records the input position through a pointer and then clears three custom chip control registers.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:$00000001:0:0072
name: copy_code_block_then_run
description: Copies about 650 bytes of its own code to a different fixed RAM address, sets two fixed RAM cells, and calls through a pointer stored in RAM. The listed facts also show a colour register write.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:SKR_1991:0:0000
name: load_hunk_executable_sections
description: Parses an AmigaDOS hunk executable, allocating memory through exec for each code, data and bss section and applying relocation records by adding the section load address to each listed longword. It ends when the end-of-file hunk type is read, and it also frees memory through exec.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:SKR_1991:0:0138
name: count_down_delay_loop
description: Decrements a 16-bit count in a register until it wraps past zero, so it burns the given number of iterations as a delay. The listed facts also show a library call and an unnamed call that the pseudo-code omits.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:SKR_1991:0:017C
name: unpack_lz_stream_backward
description: Decodes a packed stream backward into memory, alternating literal runs with back-references into output already written, with lengths read through a bit reader. It stops once the write position reaches the start of the output area.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:SKR_1991:0:01C8
name: read_bits_from_bit_buffer
description: Reads a counted number of bits from a longword bit buffer, one bit per iteration, refilling the buffer from the stream when it empties. Each bit is shifted into an accumulator register, and the routine is called by three unnamed routines.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:SKR_1991:0:021C
name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Only a trap instruction, one indexed table byte read and then invalid instruction bytes, so the decoded body is a stub and no further behaviour can be recovered.

name: setup_copper_list_and_loop
description: Boot block entry that opens the exec and graphics libraries, sets the audio channel zero and copper list pointer registers, and fills a RAM copper list with register-value pairs and a repeated block of entries. It then runs a 199-step loop that moves a signed value back and forth, waits on a flag, disables the audio DMA channels and closes the library it opened.

key: armalyte - the final run (1991)(thalamus)[cr skr](disk 1 of 2)/Armalyte - The Final Run (1991)(Thalamus)[cr SKR](Disk 1 of 2).adf:bootblock:0:0162
name: wait_for_port_then_copy
description: Waits until a hardware byte at a fixed offset reads a fixed value, then copies nine words from a table into a buffer, stepping the destination by a fixed stride. It is called by three unnamed routines and calls two more.

name: run_callback_loop_forever
description: Loops forever: each pass disables interrupts and DMA, writes a tag to RAM and points the copper list register at a fixed list. It then stores callback addresses in a fixed RAM vector cell and calls routines in a fixed sequence, and the facts show CIA interrupt control register use.

name: count_and_clear_interrupt_request
description: Increments a RAM byte and then writes a fixed bit to the interrupt request register to clear that request. It is entered from an address that the reference run executed.

name: poll_routine_until_zero
description: Calls an unnamed routine repeatedly until it returns zero, then returns. It is a polling loop with no other work.

name: wait_for_flag_then_clear
description: Busy-waits until a RAM byte becomes nonzero, then resets it to zero and returns. It is called by three unnamed routines.

name: fill_accumulating_offset_table
description: Writes two header cells from its register inputs, then fills a table with one entry per count, where each value is a running sum that grows by a fixed step. Each value's high and low words go into paired slots, and the routine returns after the last entry.

name: repeat_pair_calls_sixteen_times
description: Calls two unnamed routines per pass and repeats until a counter register reaches sixteen. It has one unnamed caller.

name: repeat_pair_calls_until_one
description: Calls two unnamed routines per pass and repeats until a counter register equals one, so it runs at least once. It has one unnamed caller.

name: scale_packed_nibble_words
description: Walks a block of words, scaling each of their three four-bit fields by a multiplier held in a register and recombining them into an output word. It is called by two unnamed routines.

name: call_library_then_run_loop
description: Makes one library call through a stored pointer, then enters the same endless loop of hardware setup and callback installation as the main segment. The listed facts show a single library call at offset minus 222.

name: call_library_entry
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then, when the zero flag is clear, calls another and invokes a library function through a pointer read from a global. It finally calls a third unnamed routine before returning.

name: open_dos_library
description: Opens a library by name through the exec OldOpenLibrary call and stores the returned handle in a global cell. The name matches the dos.library text that the facts list for this segment.

name: write_custom_registers_then_call
description: Writes the audio and disk control, DMA control, interrupt enable and request registers and the background colour register, then calls five unnamed routines. The decompiler timed out, so the values written and the order of the calls are not shown.

name: patch_code_with_jump_stubs
description: Rewrites several code locations in place, storing jump and call instructions that point at unnamed routines when a fixed check value matches, and scans a low-memory range replacing one longword pattern with a call instruction. It then calls ten unnamed routines.

name: write_jump_patch_when_set
description: Calls an unnamed routine and, when it returns a nonzero value, stores that value in a global cell and calls another routine. If the returned address is set, it also writes a jump instruction to an unnamed routine at that address.

name: store_constant_via_base
description: Stores a fixed word to a register at a fixed offset from a base pointer, then returns its input unchanged. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: find_byte_pattern_in_range
description: Scans forward from a start address toward a limit, comparing a byte pattern at each position, and returns as soon as every byte of the pattern matches. No result value is shown in the decoded body.

name: poll_right_middle_buttons
description: Accesses the pot control and pot data registers to read the right and middle button state. On one path it arms the pot output and seeds a saved state word, and on the other it clears that saved word; both paths write a fixed word to a register at a fixed offset from a base pointer.

name: reset_button_state_flag
description: Clears a saved button-state word to zero and writes a fixed word to a register at a fixed offset from a base pointer. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: patch_matching_longwords_in_range
description: Scans a memory range two bytes at a time, and wherever a longword equals one of two fixed patterns it overwrites the first word with a fixed replacement word. It stops when the scan pointer passes the end of the range.

name: return_input_unchanged
description: Returns its input register value unchanged and does nothing else. It is reached only through one address-taken reference from an unnamed caller.

name: pass_through_input_value
description: Returns its input register value unchanged and does nothing else. It is reached only through one address-taken reference from an unnamed caller.

name: set_fields_on_marker_byte
description: Compares an input byte with a fixed marker character and, when it matches, stores a fixed word and a fixed byte into two fields of a structure. Otherwise it compares the byte with a global value and returns with no change.

name: set_fields_by_base_address
description: When the input byte is the marker character, it compares the base address with five fixed addresses and, on a match, stores a fixed word and byte at the matching pair of offsets. Otherwise it returns with no change.

name: store_slot_one_fields
description: Stores a fixed word and a fixed byte at two offsets from a base address, as the first of five similar slot writers. It is entered only through an address-taken reference from one unnamed caller.

name: store_slot_two_fields
description: Stores a fixed word and a fixed byte at two offsets from a base address, as the second of five similar slot writers. It is entered only through an address-taken reference from one unnamed caller.

name: store_slot_three_fields
description: Stores a fixed word and a fixed byte at two offsets from a base address, as the third of five similar slot writers. It is entered only through an address-taken reference from one unnamed caller.

name: store_slot_four_fields
description: Stores a fixed word and a fixed byte at two offsets from a base address, as the fourth of five similar slot writers. It is entered only through an address-taken reference from one unnamed caller.

name: store_slot_five_fields
description: Stores a fixed word and a fixed byte at two offsets from a base address, as the fifth of five similar slot writers. It is entered only through an address-taken reference from one unnamed caller.

name: copy_block_to_low_ram
description: Copies 240 bytes from one fixed area to a fixed low-memory address, one byte at a time. It has no calls and no hardware writes.

name: check_shifted_byte_match
description: Shifts the input word right one bit, XORs the low byte with a fixed mask and compares the result with a global byte. It returns with no effect in either outcome, is called by three unnamed routines and calls an empty stub.

name: spin_forever_in_place
description: Loops forever doing no work, since the decoded body leaves only a bare infinite loop after removing unreachable blocks. The facts list a video beam position register read that the pseudo-code omits.

name: set_word_field_all_ones
description: Writes the all-ones word to a field at a fixed offset from a base pointer and returns. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: write_jump_entries_to_ram
description: Writes absolute jump instructions into fixed low-memory locations, each pointing at an unnamed routine, and writes one more far-memory jump the same way. It calls five unnamed routines, including one between the writes.

name: copy_block_either_direction
description: When a flag byte in a register is nonzero, it copies a 48-byte block from the caller's buffer into a fixed buffer and calls one unnamed routine. Otherwise it copies the fixed buffer back out, but only when a fixed check longword does not hold its expected value.

name: restore_block_if_unmatched
description: Copies 48 bytes from a fixed buffer to the address in a register when a fixed check longword does not hold its expected value. Otherwise it returns with no copy.

name: wait_port_bit_when_flagged
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then if a RAM count is nonzero it busy-waits while a port status bit stays set. It returns the result of the first routine.

name: relay_to_unnamed_routine
description: Calls one unnamed routine and returns, with no other work. It is entered through an address-taken reference and called by four unnamed routines.

name: call_library_or_return_zero
description: Stores a character derived from a register in a RAM cell, then calls a library entry through a base pointer and returns its result when it is non-negative. Otherwise it calls one unnamed routine and returns zero; the facts list the text disk.

name: xor_longwords_with_key
description: XORs each longword in a block with a key held in a register, stepping four bytes at a time until the byte count is used up. It has one unnamed caller.

name: unpack_control_byte_stream
description: Decodes a control-byte compressed stream into memory, handling literal copies, back-references of two lengths and repeat-fill runs until the output pointer reaches its end. It first copies a preset window of bytes into the output when a count is nonzero, and finishes by calling an unnamed routine and a library entry.

name: call_unnamed_routine_undecoded
description: The pseudo-code is unavailable, so the only evidence is an eleven-instruction body that makes one call to an unnamed routine. No further behaviour can be stated from the listed facts.

name: transfer_scores_block_capped
description: Sets a fixed check longword, then calls a library entry to transfer up to 48 bytes into a fixed buffer. It caps the returned count at 48, calls a second library entry when that count is nonzero, and returns the count and its complement; the facts list the text scores.sav.

name: transfer_scores_block_plain
description: Calls a library entry at a fixed offset with a 48-byte buffer and returns the complement of its result. The facts list the text scores.sav, and whether the call reads or writes is not shown.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: A single return instruction with no other effect, so the routine is an empty stub. It is reached only as an executed entry in the reference run.

name: decrunch_backward_bit_stream
description: Checks a four-byte signature at the start of the input, then decodes a backward bit stream of literal bytes and back-references, with lengths and distances taken from small code tables. It works from the end of the buffer toward the start and stops once the output reaches the beginning.

name: plot_pixel_across_bitplanes
description: Plots one pixel into a multi-plane bitmap after bounds checks, computing the word address from the coordinates and then setting, clearing or XORing the bit in each enabled plane according to a mode flag. The facts list a single instruction for the entry, but the pseudo-code shows the full body.

name: call_then_spin_when_flagged
description: When a RAM word is nonzero, calls one unnamed routine, spins in a loop whose exit test can never succeed, and then calls another unnamed routine. The facts list one instruction for the entry, which the pseudo-code does not match.

name: copy_table_and_reset_state
description: Clears a RAM word, copies 128 longwords from a fixed table into a buffer pointed to by a global, sets a global control value to fifteen and returns zero. It is reached only as a gap in the decoded segment.

name: load_sound_module_header
description: Copies a 128-longword header block from the given address into a fixed table. When a four-byte signature matches, it rebases the pointers in that table by the load address and clears four 20-word state blocks, returning success; otherwise it returns minus one.

name: init_module_playback_state
description: Rebases pointers in a module block by the load address, clears four 20-word state blocks and sets up pattern pointers. It also writes a low-nibble value to a DMA control register through a base pointer and returns with no value.

name: initialize_dma_table_and_state
description: Clears a global variable, copies 128 longwords from a fixed address into a table pointed to by a global, sets another global to a constant and returns zero. The listed facts also show DMA control and vertical beam position register use.

name: relay_two_unnamed_calls
description: Calls two unnamed routines in sequence and returns. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: advance_music_tick_voices
description: Counts down a tick counter and, on each expiry, walks the four voice records and applies each record's effect command to its volume and pitch fields. The facts also list a write to the audio channel zero location register.

name: run_voice_effect_loop
description: Runs a per-tick loop over the voice records that applies slide, volume and pitch commands and advances each voice's counters, returning once every voice is done. It has its own entry point at the start of the routine.

name: enter_voice_effect_loop
description: Copies a pitch field from a voice record into a second field, then enters the same per-voice effect loop as its neighbouring routine. The facts list one unnamed caller.

name: read_next_voice_events
description: Walks the four voice records and, for each whose countdown has reached zero, reads the next event from its stream and stores longwords from a table into the record. Otherwise it decrements the countdown and moves on, and it calls two unnamed routines.

name: update_voice_outputs_per_frame
description: Clears a pending flag, writes a saved DMA word and waits on a loop tied to the beam position before setting an interrupt enable pattern. It then advances a per-voice counter, reloading four table pointers when it expires, and copies each voice's pointer and length pair into its output cells.

name: process_voices_and_set_dma
description: Clears a byte in a voice record and enters the per-voice loop, which copies each record's pointer and length into its outputs. When the loop ends it writes the combined DMA enable bits to the DMA control register and stores them in a state byte.

name: set_voice_trigger_then_process
description: Stores a trigger byte into two fields of a voice block, with a special case for the value one, and then enters the same per-voice processing loop that writes the combined DMA enable bits. It is a short entry point into that shared loop.

name: update_audio_channel_and_minimums
description: Decrements a counter and, when it goes negative, resets it and calls one unnamed routine. It keeps four minimum values updated from an extracted field, and when a flag equals minus one it copies four audio channel blocks into the audio channel registers.

name: step_channels_then_run_setup
description: Repeatedly steps channel values toward their targets through calls to unnamed routines, writes a DMA control value, and then runs a sequence of setup calls through library pointers. It returns an error code with a fixed flag bit set when one of those steps fails; the pseudo-code is partly unreliable for this long routine.

name: run_setup_steps_if_ok
description: Calls one library entry through a base pointer and, when its result is non-negative, performs three setup calls on an address and returns the result of one more call. Otherwise it returns the result with a fixed flag bit set.

name: fade_palette_toward_targets
description: Steps each of 32 colour entries toward a target colour one four-bit channel at a time, writing the results to the colour registers, and repeats while a flag is clear. It calls two unnamed routines per pass and returns once a pass makes no change.

name: copy_table_then_zero_range
description: Copies 32 words from one table to another, then clears a run of words starting at an index held in a register for a count held in another register. It then calls one unnamed routine.

name: copy_table_then_fill_run
description: Copies 32 words between two tables, then fills a run of words starting at an index in a register with the first copied word. It writes a fixed value to a global cell, calls one unnamed routine, and the listed facts show a DMA control register write.

name: write_request_and_wait
description: Writes a fixed word to a request field of a structure, waits while a status word in it stays nonzero, then calls one unnamed routine with its own address and another with the structure pointer. The listed facts show only these calls and field accesses.

name: step_selector_from_port_bits
description: Checks two high bits of a port state byte and resets a selector to one when they are not both set, then steps the selector up or down. The step up calls a routine through a table entry, and the facts list the fire-button and disk status register.

name: wait_until_word_exceeds
description: Busy-waits while a RAM word is less than or equal to the value in a register, returning once it exceeds that value. It has one unnamed caller.

name: allocate_block_and_report_status
description: Requests a block of four thousand bytes through a library entry at a base pointer, stores the returned pointer, calls one unnamed routine and clears a status word. It returns a result byte with a fixed flag bit set when a second status word is nonzero.

name: clear_status_word
description: Clears one status word at a fixed offset from a base pointer and returns. It is reached only as a gap in the decoded segment.

name: read_joystick_and_mouse_ports
description: Reads the mouse and joystick movement registers and the fire-button register, converts their bits into direction and button states through lookup tables, and accumulates movement values clamped to a fixed ceiling. The decoded branches are partly unreliable, so only this overall role is stated.

name: call_handler_table_then_clear
description: Clears a RAM cell, calls each non-null entry of an eight-entry pointer table in turn, and then writes a fixed bit to the interrupt request register. The listed facts show that register touch.

name: stub_no_decoded_function
description: The decompiler produced no function for this two-instruction gap, so no behaviour can be recovered from the listed evidence.

name: plot_pixel_with_mode_flag
description: Plots one pixel into a multi-plane bitmap after bounds checks, then sets, clears or XORs the matching bit in each enabled plane, with a separate branch for XOR mode. The facts show 103 instructions for this routine.

name: copy_dos_stream_until_empty
description: Clears a byte at the end of a buffer, opens a file through dos.library and repeats a read-and-write step while the read returns a positive count, then closes the file. The entry point also opens and closes a library through exec.

name: call_table_entry_then_store
description: Program entry that calls a table entry through a pointer and, when the result is nonzero, calls a library function at offset minus 210. It then writes a fixed longword to a RAM cell and stores a saved value at a computed address, and the facts also show a call to an empty stub.

name: unpack_coded_block_stream
description: Program entry that copies a table of longword groups into memory, then decodes bit-coded lengths and back-copies bytes within the output. It stops when the table reaches a negative marker, and it calls three unnamed routines along the way.

name: select_half_or_input
description: Returns its input word unchanged unless a flag register equals one, in which case it returns half of a second register word. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: lookup_masked_table_word
description: Looks up a word in a table at a fixed base, indexed by twice a register value, and returns it masked with a second register word. The facts also list a call to a countdown routine, which the pseudo-code omits.

name: call_table_entry_then_patch
description: Program entry that calls a table entry through a pointer and, when the result is nonzero, calls a library function at offset minus 210. It then writes a fixed longword to a RAM cell and stores a saved value at a computed address, and the facts also show a call to an empty stub.

name: stub_return_immediately
description: A single return with no effect, so the routine is an empty stub. It is entered by address through one unnamed reference.

name: decode_packed_words_to_memory
description: Decodes a packed stream into memory with a carry-driven bit reader, copying literal words and back-references and filling from a table of longword pointers. It stops at a sentinel word of all ones and then runs a short delay; the facts also list the text S404.

key: fate - gates of dawn (1991)(reline)[cr fsn][f lsa](disk 1 of 3)/Fate - Gates of Dawn (1991)(reLINE)[cr FSN][f LSA](Disk 1 of 3).adf:FATE:1:007E
name: stub_empty_routine_entry
description: The decoded body is only a return, although the facts list two unnamed calls and four unnamed callers, so the routine's effect is not recovered.

name: decode_packed_blocks_with_alloc
description: Decodes a packed stream backward into memory with a bit reader, allocating a memory block through exec for each table entry and copying literal words and back-references into the output. It stops at a sentinel word of all ones and then runs a short delay.

name: apply_longword_relocations_table
description: Walks a table of offset entries and adds a base value to the longword at each offset, returning when the table reaches its end marker. The facts also list a library call at a fixed offset and two unnamed calls.

name: spin_countdown_delay
description: Runs an empty countdown loop from a value passed in a register, then returns. It is called by two unnamed routines.

name: call_pair_with_colour_write
description: Nine-instruction routine that writes the background colour register and makes two calls to unnamed routines. The decompiler timed out, so no further detail is shown.

name: init_vectors_and_copy_block
description: Sets a few fixed low-memory cells to constant values, waits for a RAM byte to clear and writes a series of configuration values to the CIA and custom chip control registers listed in the facts. It then copies a block of about 3.4 kilobytes from one fixed address to low RAM and returns.

name: write_interrupt_request_value
description: Writes a fixed value to the interrupt request register and returns. The facts list that register touch and no other effect.

name: store_three_values_to_ram
description: Stores two register parameters and one stacked value into three fixed RAM cells and returns. It is entered by address through one unnamed caller.

name: open_library_install_interrupt_handler
description: Opens a library through exec and saves the previous value of a handler field. If that saved value was zero it restores the field, closes the library and returns zero; otherwise it installs a routine as the handler, writes an interrupt enable value and spins forever.

name: program_cia_timer_from_constant
description: Opens a named resource through exec and programs a CIA timer by dividing a constant by 125 and writing its low and high bytes to a CIA data block with an enable bit set. It retries with a second constant when the first attempt fails and returns the timer count when a step succeeds.

name: clear_cia_bit_and_call
description: If a RAM cell is nonzero, clears it, clears an enable bit in a CIA control block and calls a library entry at a fixed offset. It does nothing when the cell is zero, and it has two unnamed callers.

name: start_cia_timer_from_value
description: Writes the low and high bytes of a RAM value into one of two CIA timer register blocks chosen by a flag, then sets the control register to start the timer. It returns its input registers unchanged.

name: load_cia_timer_and_start
description: Writes the low and high bytes of a register word into one CIA timer block and sets the control register to start it, returning its input unchanged. It has one unnamed caller.

name: dispatch_indexed_handler_entry
description: Calls one unnamed routine, then calls an entry from a table selected by a RAM index, and writes a fixed value to the interrupt request register. The facts list that register touch and one unnamed call.

name: copy_selected_bits_across_planes
description: Walks a sequence of bit positions taken from a table indexed by a RAM value, wrapping at a fixed size, and for each of four planes copies the selected bit from a source plane into a destination plane. The beam position register read in the facts does not appear in the decoded loop.

name: initialize_structure_fields
description: Calls one unnamed routine and, when its condition flag is clear, fills a structure with two code addresses and zeroed fields, writes a constant to a global cell, calls another unnamed routine and returns one. Otherwise it returns the first call's result.

name: decrement_field_if_nonzero
description: Decrements a word field at a fixed offset from a base pointer when it is nonzero, and returns. It is reached only as a gap in the decoded segment.

name: blit_string_rows_to_bitmap
description: Waits for a RAM flag to clear, programs the blitter control, modulo, pointer and size registers, and copies rows from a lookup table for each character of a zero-terminated byte string. A character code of ten moves the destination to the next line.

name: step_colour_nibbles_over_passes
description: Adjusts each four-bit colour channel of a table by one step toward a target, waiting on a RAM flag between passes and deriving a pass count from a division of a RAM value. It repeats for the number of passes given in a register and then returns.

name: save_dma_and_intena_state
description: Loads two pointers from a structure, calls several library entries and one unnamed routine, then saves the DMA control and interrupt enable read-back values with the set bit added. The facts list the custom register reads behind those saved values.

name: call_library_pair_and_set
description: Calls two library entries through a base pointer and writes a value to the copper list pointer, DMA control and interrupt enable registers through global cells. The facts list those register writes.

name: run_supervisor_if_flagged
description: When a flag bit in a structure is set, calls the exec Supervisor entry through a base pointer and returns its result; otherwise it returns zero. It is called by one unnamed routine.

name: build_copper_list_and_start
description: Fills three display pointer entries from a base address, stepping by a fixed row size, and builds a 200-entry copper list of register-value pairs in RAM. It then writes the list address, the copper jump register and the beam control values; the facts list those register writes.

name: store_offset_result_pair
description: Calls one unnamed routine and stores its result in two global cells, one with a fixed offset added. It has one unnamed caller and calls one more unnamed routine.

name: allocate_tracked_block_slot
description: Finds a free two-word slot in a table ending with a sentinel, allocates a memory block through exec for the size in a register, and records the block's pointer and size in that slot. It returns the pointer, or zero when no slot or memory is available.

name: free_tracked_block_slots
description: Walks the two-word slot table and, for each occupied slot that matches a requested pointer or every slot when none is given, clears the slot and frees its memory through exec. It stops after one match when a specific pointer was requested.

name: update_four_record_positions
description: Refreshes four entries of a record table from a source table, adjusting their positions by a per-record step and wrapping them at a stored limit. It then clears a block of 32 forty-byte records when a flag is set, and calls four unnamed routines; the facts list a DMA control read.

name: set_bits_from_table_column
description: When a flag is nonzero, sets single bits in a bitmap plane for four rows of table values, computing each row offset from the value and a count clamped to a fixed limit. The facts list one unnamed call.

name: store_channel_table_entry
description: Writes pointer values derived from a source record into a 16-byte entry of a table selected by an index field, computing addresses from two word fields. It clears one pointer when the second field equals one and calls one unnamed routine.

name: reset_audio_channels_pointers
description: When a RAM value is set, computes a limit from a 128-byte table, fills a 30-entry pointer table from a structure's step fields and writes a control value to a global cell. It then zeroes the four audio volume registers and writes a low-nibble value to the DMA control register.

name: zero_audio_volumes_and_dma
description: Writes zero to the four audio volume registers, writes a low-nibble value to the DMA control register through a global cell, and returns its input register unchanged.

name: open_library_then_copy_block
description: Opens a library through exec, disables interrupts and task switching, calls two unnamed routines and a short delay, then copies about 3.4 kilobytes from a table to a fixed RAM address. On one path it also writes beam control and DMA values and calls a library entry before returning.

name: wrap_supervisor_call_flagged
description: When a second flag bit in a structure is set, calls one unnamed routine and then the exec Supervisor entry through a base pointer. The facts list a wrapper that calls Supervisor and returns its result.

name: copy_block_to_fixed_address
description: Copies about 3.4 kilobytes from a table to a fixed RAM address, one byte at a time, then calls one unnamed routine and returns. It is entered by address through one unnamed caller.

name: scan_and_unpack_tagged_blocks
description: Allocates memory through exec and walks a linked list of blocks, and for each block carrying a specific four-byte tag it copies data backward and runs a decoding loop through unnamed routines. It returns minus three when the allocation fails.

name: extract_flag_bit_from_table
description: Scans a table of word pairs until a masked value matches the pair's second word, then uses a byte from the matching entry as a bit index to extract a bit from a mask and set a result bit. It calls one unnamed routine when a signed byte comparison overflows.

name: mask_and_conditional_call
description: Masks one word with another and, when a signed byte comparison shows the first byte is smaller than the second, calls an unnamed routine and returns its word instead. Otherwise it returns the masked word, and it is called by two unnamed routines.

name: return_empty_routine
description: The routine is empty and returns at once without changing memory or registers. It is called by two unnamed routines.

name: accumulate_32bit_from_bytes
description: Reads four consecutive bytes from the address in a register and concatenates them into a 32-bit value that it returns. The routine is reached only as a gap in the decoded segment.

name: build_length_code_table
description: Reads a count and a list of code lengths from a stack buffer, then loops over bit lengths one to sixteen, writing for each length a bit mask, a bit-reversed code value and a derived limit into a table. It makes one unnamed call to read each value.

name: apply_hunk_relocations
description: When a block's first longword equals the hunk relocation type code, clears it and walks the relocation entries of the following hunk, adding each hunk's base address to the longwords at the listed offsets. The facts also list an exec FreeMem call.

name: copy_sixteen_longwords_then_call
description: If a destination pointer taken from the stack is not null, copies sixteen longwords from a fixed offset to that destination, then calls through a pointer held in a register. It is called by one unnamed routine and calls one more.

name: scan_blocks_and_copy_backward
description: Allocates memory through exec and walks a linked list of blocks, and for each block carrying a specific four-byte tag it copies a region backward eight longwords at a time before running a decoding loop through unnamed routines. It returns minus four when the allocation fails.

name: extract_flag_bit_from_table
description: Scans a table of word pairs until a masked value matches the pair's second word, then uses a byte from the matching entry as a bit index to extract a bit from a mask and set a result bit. It calls one unnamed routine when a signed byte comparison overflows.

name: mask_and_conditional_call
description: Masks one word with another and, when a signed byte comparison shows the first byte is smaller than the second, calls an unnamed routine and returns its word instead. Otherwise it returns the masked word, and it is called by two unnamed routines.

name: return_empty_routine
description: The routine is empty and returns at once without changing memory or registers. It is called by two unnamed routines.

name: build_length_code_table
description: Reads a count and a list of code lengths from a stack buffer, then loops over bit lengths one to sixteen, writing for each length a bit mask, a bit-reversed code value and a derived limit into a table. It makes one unnamed call to read each value.

name: apply_hunk_relocations
description: When a block's first longword equals the hunk relocation type code, clears it and walks the relocation entries of the following hunk, adding each hunk's base address to the longwords at the listed offsets. The facts also list an exec FreeMem call.

name: return_empty_routine
description: The routine is empty and returns at once without changing memory or registers. It is entered by address through one unnamed reference.

name: initialize_custom_chips_and_copper
description: Program entry that clears a block of memory, builds a copper list and sprite pointer tables, writes the interrupt and DMA enable masks, and waits on the video position register while stepping a counter. It restores the saved copper and interrupt values before returning, and the facts also list audio volume register writes.

name: handle_keyboard_status_byte
description: Checks a keyboard status byte: when bit three is set it writes 255 to a RAM byte if the status byte equals the letter v, then loops indefinitely, and otherwise it stores eight in a structure field. The facts list the keyboard serial register.

name: build_glyph_table_entries
description: Reads characters from a zero-terminated string and, for each non-space character, copies eight rows of font data from a font table into a buffer with rows 40 bytes apart. Space characters only advance the column, and at the end it stores a width word derived from the byte after the terminator.

name: store_three_header_fields
description: Stores a RAM address and two constants into a structure pointed to by a register, followed by a third constant word. It returns with no other work.

name: update_frame_scroll_and_palette
description: Adjusts a scroll counter and a fade value with a per-frame step, fills a short run of colour entries with a value built from a nibble, and waits for the blitter to be idle before programming blitter registers and storing bitplane pointer halves in a RAM list. The facts list the DMA control write and two unnamed calls.

name: toggle_bitmap_arc_bits
description: Steps a counter through 65 values, computes the difference of two squares, and uses a table lookup to choose a row and bit. It XOR-toggles that bit in one of two bitmap planes at mirrored positions, chosen by a flag, and makes no calls.

name: parse_command_string_startup
description: Program entry that allocates and fills a message through exec, finds its own task and parses a command string from the message, handling quoted text and star escapes such as newline and escape codes. It opens files through dos and may wait on a message port, returning a status code of twenty when the message allocation fails; the facts also list the text NIL: and dos.library.

name: clean_up_saved_state
description: Stores its parameter in a structure reached through a global pointer, then conditionally calls cleanup entries that close files and libraries and reply to a message, depending on which stored handles are nonzero. It returns the saved parameter.
